subject: Hosted evaluation: quickstart & traffic thresholds (ClearPay)

Subject: Hosted evaluation: quickstart & traffic thresholds (ClearPay)

Hi Tanya — great conversation this morning, thanks for walking us through the use case. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can get your Hosted evaluation standing up quickly: 

High-level recap
- Goal: production pilot for conversational payments assistant (FAQ + guided flows) for US customers by end of Q4.
- Desired SLO: p95 < 800ms for user-facing single-turn requests; prefer lower for short-turn confirmations.
- Data residency: US only; no sensitive PII in training but some payment tokens in payloads (we'll work on redaction).

Requests we need from you to size a Hosted trial (attached a CSV template):
1) Expected daily QPS and peak burst (5-min window) per endpoint — please use the attached sample_traffic_profile.csv.
2) Typical prompt + generation token sizes (avg and 95th pct).
3) Concurrency tolerance — how many parallel user sessions do you expect to maintain?
4) Any hard constraints on cost or need for private network (VPC) now vs later.

Quickstart and what we can deliver on Hosted (what we will set up)
- Trial API key + three sandbox endpoints (assistant-short, assistant-long, reranker)
- Rate cap configured per-endpoint; default pipeline includes prefix caching and token-level batching.
- Monitoring dashboard access (latency/cost/requests) and a dedicated Slack channel for ops.

Proposed immediate next steps
- You: fill sample_traffic_profile.csv and return by EOD Monday.
- Us: provision sandbox endpoints and send demo credentials within 24 hours of receiving the traffic profile.
- Follow-up call: 30 minutes to review dashboard and confirm rate caps (we can do Tues/Wed next week).

Attachments: sample_traffic_profile.csv (CSV template), SOW-draft.pdf (high-level pilot scope)

Thanks — looping in Aditya for technical sizing and Marcus for the commercial/credits side.

— Sofia
Sofia Ivanova

Subject: Re: Hosted evaluation: quickstart & traffic thresholds (ClearPay)

Thanks Sofia — appreciated the recap. I filled the key numbers inline below and attached the CSV with the traffic rows. Short answers first, details in the file.

Traffic snapshot (current production, Q2)
- Avg daily requests (all endpoints): ~120,000/day
- Average concurrent sessions (business hours): ~18
- Peak 5-min burst observed: ~48 QPS (holiday promo bursts were higher but rare)
- Endpoint split: 60% assistant-short, 30% assistant-long, 10% reranker

Token sizes
- assistant-short: prompt 180 tokens, gen 90 tokens (avg ~270)
- assistant-long: prompt 450 tokens, gen 220 tokens (avg ~670)
- reranker: single-turn snippets ~120 tokens total

SLOs and tolerance
- Target: p95 < 800ms for assistant-short; p95 < 1.2s acceptable for assistant-long.
- If we see sustained throttling, we need an SLA-backed option (we have procurement conversations that prefer Dedicated only if sustained >150k/day or concurrency >40).

Notes: we can redact payment tokens client-side, and we do not require an on-prem option for the pilot.

I'll attach the CSV (sent). Available for the Tuesday follow-up 11:00–12:00 PT.

Best,
Tanya
Head of Platform Engineering, ClearPay
T: 415-555-2244

Subject: Re: Hosted evaluation: quickstart & traffic thresholds (ClearPay)

Thanks for the numbers, Tanya — those are very helpful. A few technical recommendations and clarifications to make the Hosted pilot smooth: 

Sizing guidance (recommended Hosted configuration)
- Endpoints: keep the three endpoints (short/long/reranker). We'll map them to separate backend model pools so batching and caching are optimized per profile.
- Concurrency target: configure soft concurrency at 30 for assistant-short and 12 for assistant-long. This gives headroom for batching without high queuing latency.
- Rate caps: set per-endpoint caps -> assistant-short 60 QPS, assistant-long 12 QPS, reranker 10 QPS. These map to a conservative initial limit given your peak 48 QPS split. We can increase once we see production patterns.
- Tokenization/Model: recommend quantized 7B family (Redwood-7B-quant) for assistant-short for latency/cost balance; assistant-long can run on a variant tuned for long context.

Performance knobs (Hosted-specific)
- Enable KV/prefix caching for repeated prompts (payments confirmations often repeat templates). This can reduce cost by ~25–40% for identical prefixes.
- Continuous batching window: 10–20ms to preserve p50 latency while getting batching benefits.
- Burst handling: we will set auto-burst allowance (short-duration overage) to handle holiday spikes; sustained >150k/day triggers a review and Dedicated recommendation.

Quickstart steps we will take once CSV is received
1) Provision sandbox API key and the three endpoints (24h).
2) Pre-warm model pools with small synthetic load mirroring your average prompt sizes (we ask for a 1-hour replay sample).
3) Push dashboard invite and initial rate policy; monitor first 48h and revise caps.

One operational ask: can you provide a 1-hour request replay (anonymized) or a small log extract (JSON lines) so we can pre-warm with realistic sequences? If you prefer, we can sign an NDA for logs but given the data is already redacted on your side we should be fine.

If everything looks good I'll sign off on the sandbox provisioning as soon as I get the filled CSV + short replay sample.

— Aditya
